intro: Take a breath: you are at 1,500 m. This is Sagalassos, an ancient city in Burdur province, whose story begins in the 5th century BC. It is a mountain city, famous for its restored fountain — and that fountain still flows.
history: Sagalassos held the title 'first city of Pisidia', and it exported fine tableware across the empire. Then, in the 6th century, earthquake and plague emptied it.
structure-1: Now you stand before the Antonine Nymphaeum, the monumental fountain on the north side of the Upper Agora. A long basin lies in front, and behind it a wall divided by columned niches, a half-domed apse in the middle and statues in the niches. Its fallen blocks were set up again where they lay, and after some 1,700 years it runs with water once more. The model shows it with its water and its statues, in the everyday life of the square.
structure-2: You are now in the Upper Agora, the main civic and commercial square at the centre of the city. Imagine it full of voices, trade and town business.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Theatre, the Heroon and the Roman Baths.
facts: Did you know? The restored Antonine fountain flows again after 1,700 dry years. Fragments of a colossal Hadrian were found here, including a foot and a head each over a metre and a half. And because the city was abandoned after earthquakes and plague and never built over, its plan survives undisturbed.
outro: This brings our tour of Sagalassos to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This mountain city has waited for centuries; let it keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
